entries.title: The three jobs of a sign
entries.html:
One picture can work in three ways. The house plan shows all three.

JobExampleReadsHow it works
word-signprmeans what it shows, “house”; the stroke says “take the picture literally”
sound-signprjspells the sounds p + r in another word, “go out”; the mouth confirms the r
determinative(silent)tags the kind of word, here movement, and marks where the word ends

entries.title: Which way to read
entries.html: Read into the faces. People, animals and birds look toward the start of the line. Columns are read from top to bottom, and the faces tell you which column comes first. Books, and the ΙΕΡΟΓΛΥΦΩ editor, usually print left to right; monuments often run right to left.

entries.title: Phonetic complements
entries.html:
A one-consonant sign that repeats a sound of the big sign just before it is a complement: a reading aid, read only once.

WrittenReadsEcho
ꜥnḫthe ankh is ꜥnḫ by itself; n and ḫ repeat its last sounds
jmnthe game board is mn; the water n repeats its last sound

entries.title: Common determinatives
entries.html:
A determinative is never read aloud and never transliterated. It says what kind of word you are reading, and since it stands last, it shows where the word ends.

SignTags words forExample
men, their names and jobs zꜣ “son”
women and their names zꜣt “daughter”
gods, sometimes the king Ptḥ “Ptah”
eating, speaking, thinking, feeling ḥqr “hunger”
movement hꜣj “go down”
force and effort nḫt “strong”
buildings and rooms ꜥt “room”
towns and cities Mn-nfr “Memphis”
deserts and foreign lands Kꜣš “Kush”
the sun, light, time rk “time, age”
writing, and ideas you can’t draw rḫ “know”
small, weak or bad things šrj “small”

entries.title: More than one, and gods first
entries.html:
You seeIt means
three strokes or after a wordmore than one: read the plural ending, usually w
a sign written three times, the older, grander plural: nṯrw “gods”
a sign written twice, two of a kind, the dual: tꜣwj “the Two Lands”
a god, “god” or “king” written firsthonorific transposition: often read last, as in mdw-nṯr “the god’s words”

Don’t swap blindly: in Jmn-ḥtp “Amun is content” the god really is the first word.

entries.title: The 25 letters, and how to type them
entries.html: The alphabet page lists all 25 one-consonant signs in dictionary order, with their sounds: ꜣ j y ꜥ w b p f m n r h ḥ ḫ ẖ z s š q k g t ṯ d ḏ. To type the special letters, use the plain-keyboard codes A i a H x X S T D for ꜣ j ꜥ ḥ ḫ ẖ š ṯ ḏ.

The sḏm.f: read the word in front
A verb that describes a noun

rows.is: a stroke under a sign: it is a word-sign, read it as the thing it shows
a sign at the end that you can’t read: a determinative, silent
a sound written twice: a phonetic complement, read it once
three strokes: a plural, add the ending (usually w)
a sign written three times: an old-style plural
a sign written twice: a dual, two of a kind
a god or a king written first: honorific transposition, often read last
